items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4330

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to
establishing a wood products development council


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
This bill would create a Wood Products Development Council within the
New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Section 1 amends section 16 of the agriculture and markets law to
expand the powers and duties of the Department to include encouraging
and supporting the practice of forestry and the manufacture of wood
products.

Section 2 of the bill adds a new article 18 to the agriculture and
markets law creating the Wood Products Council, providing for its
membership and directing it to, among other things, work with
wood-using manufacturers to increase the economic vitality of the wood
products industry.

 JUSTIFICATION :
The Wood Products Development Council will provide economic, social,
and environmental benefits for New York, while improving the
effectiveness of government programs and the quality of life in
upstate communities. Since the late nineteenth century, the size of
New York's forest has increased steadily to the point where over 60%
of the state is now covered by forest, a forest is distinguished by
its variety and quality hardwoods. About 47,000 New Yorkers work in
the forest products industry, earning approximately $2 billion in
high-paying jobs in small rural communities.

In an era of an increasing level of international trade, New York's
hardwood forests can readily provide exports to worldwide markets with
strong demand for our forest products.  Yet even though the growth,
manufacture, and sale of forest products is a key component of the
upstate economy, New York is missing a significant opportunity for
economic growth, because there is no coordination between
stakeholders, to maximize, nurture, and manage this critical resource.
Increasing New York's hardwood forest industry would provide more good
paying jobs and invigorate the economies of rural communities. The
industry is characterized by family and multigenerational ownerships.
It also has strong economic development multipliers, as the production
of forest products requires highly-skilled and knowledge-based support
in engineering and logistics.

Forest products link value-added manufacturing and processing with
environmental good sense because the industry serves as a steward of
our forests. Just like agriculture, proper forestry is a stewardship
practice, yielding clean water and air, removing greenhouse gases, and
preventing or mitigating natural disasters like floods and wildfire.

This bill creates a Wood Products Development Council to work closely
with the state's leading rural economic development agency, the
Department of Agriculture and Markets.  Representing all stakeholders,
from lumber to maple syrup, from forest owners to furniture
manufacturers, the Council would advise the Governor on forest
products policy, raise public awareness of the benefits of a healthy
forest products industry, provide technical assistance to forest
product businesses, help ensure that forest resources are put to
beneficial use, and develop the wider value-added forest product
industry.


Numerous policy initiatives have pointed to the need for this level of
recognition and coordination. The Governor's Task Force on the Forest
Industry and the Northern Forest Lands Council identified the
opportunities. New York's Open Space Place recognizes the important
role that the forest products industry plays in helping to support
family and working forests.

Pennsylvania has had a Hardwoods Development Council since 1988, and
has successfully increased that state's exports of hardwood products
across the country and abroad.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
Minimal as it allows for the reimbursement of board members for their
actual and necessary travel expenses.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.
